content.comment_body: I want to use [product_name] Access Tool to read data in Excel, but since it only supports connecting to one PLC, I need to collect data from multiple PLCs in the network into one device. There are two UP/DOWN counters and an hour counter, but I don't know how to begin retrieving the data over the network. Can anyone offer some guidance on where to search?
Are you referring to having a second PLC, as in another [product_name] device?
Yes, I am talking about using a second [product_name].

This can be achieved using Parameter VM Mapping. You need to add both [product_name] units into a network project and establish a connection between them. Then, with Parameter VM Mapping, you can transfer the values from the counters and the hour counter to the second [product_name]. The Access Tool on this device can then read all the required data. To retrieve data in the Access Tool, you can use formulas such as: Counter 1 -> = LOGOVAR ("VD0"), Counter 2 -> = LOGOVAR ("VD4"), Hours Counter -> = LOGOVAR ("VD8").

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to gather data from more than one PLC but faces a restriction since [product_name] Access Tool supports only a single device at a time. A more experienced user suggests using network project setup and Parameter VM Mapping between multiple [product_name] modules to centralize and extract counter values. This exchange underlines a common challenge for users attempting to aggregate distributed automation data efficiently.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a straightforward method to read and combine data from several PLCs across a network into one device for processing in Excel, ideally with minimal complexity.
pain_keywords: unclear setup for network data readout
